subject: Food Science
title: Food Fraud
description: A micro-lesson that makes Food Fraud usable.

hook.text: 70% of extra-virgin olive oil sold in the US fails purity tests. Much of it is cut with cheaper seed oils.

buildup.text: Food fraud is intentional deception for economic gain: dilution, substitution, mislabeling, or counterfeiting of food products.

discovery.text: Honey is the third most faked food globally. Cheap corn syrup is added and pollen is filtered out to hide geographic origin.

twist.text: Seafood fraud is rampant: DNA testing reveals 30% of fish in US restaurants is mislabeled—cheap tilapia sold as red snapper.

climax.text: The 2013 European horse meat scandal found horse DNA in beef products across 13 countries. Trust in food supply chains collapsed.

punchline.text: If the price looks too good, the food might be too fake. Fraud hides in every aisle.

quiz.question: What percentage of fish in US restaurants is mislabeled according to DNA testing?
